mostWorthwhile.text: Following metal droplets as gravity separated them into an iron-rich core made differentiation tangible, especially with the clarification that other pathways are possible.

leastWorthwhile.text: Combining sinking metal with the magma ocean felt somewhat repetitive after the preceding separation step, although it completed the core sequence.

surprise.text: The result clarified that metal could reach the interior through several pathways, including droplets and large impactor cores.

arbitrary.text: Combining the already-sinking metal with Earth again had a clear goal but felt less physically distinct than the gravity step.

continue.text: Yes. The clear physical explanations and the temporary crust leave me curious how later impacts reshape the planet, though the largely linear choices were less engaging.
